key_insight: Open-weight, locally run LLM agents can nearly automate complex longitudinal data-preparation workflows without sending sensitive research data to the cloud.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical pathway for governance-restricted studies to use AI-assisted code generation and data cleaning on consumer-grade hardware.
method: Built an open-source benchmark from ground-truth R scripts for six sweeps of a British cohort study.
Defined 20 data-preparation tasks, including category harmonization and multi-wave merging, spanning 102 variables.
Evaluated LLM-generated R code and resulting outputs with automated scoring routines.
evidence_signal: In the benchmark, state-of-the-art 31–35B open-weight models nearly saturated performance, reaching up to 87.9% average task completion.
watch_item: Strong benchmark results may not fully translate to messy real-world datasets, where edge cases, domain rules, and verification overhead can still limit safe deployment.
paper_title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks
